common_name: Betty Rice Daylily (Powder Pink-Lavender Blend, Ancestor of Minted Gold)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this dormant diploid, registered by Fay-Russell in 1956, opens powder pink and lavender blend flowers in the midseason-to-late period.

directions: Registered by Fay-Russell in 1956, Betty Rice is a dormant diploid daylily bearing a blend of powder pink and lavender, about five inches across on 36-inch scapes with extended bloom habit that open in the midseason-to-late period. It carries no AHS awards of its own, but it became a breeding-line staple through the Fay and Reckamp lines of the 1960s, passing its blend coloring forward through daughter plants such as Crestwood Ann. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Crestwood Ann Daylily (Medium Melon Self, Ancestor of Minted Gold)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this dormant tetraploid, registered by Fay-Griesbach in 1961 from a cross of Betty Rice and a seedling, opens a medium melon self flower with extended bloom habit in the early midseason.

directions: Registered by Fay-Griesbach in 1961 from a cross of Betty Rice and an unnamed seedling, Crestwood Ann is a dormant tetraploid bearing a medium melon self flower on 25-inch scapes with extended bloom habit that open in the early midseason. Carried under the seedling number T-59-24, it carries no AHS awards of its own. Its parentage through Betty Rice later fed into Reckamp's gold-toned breeding program, including the tetraploid Minted Gold. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Shooting Star Daylily (Light Yellow Self, Ancestor of Minted Gold)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this dormant diploid, registered by D.F. Hall in 1951, opens light yellow, wide-petaled, recurving flowers with diurnal bloom habit in the midseason-to-late period.

directions: Registered by D.F. Hall in 1951, Shooting Star is a dormant diploid daylily bearing a light yellow self flower with wide, recurving petals, carried on 38-inch scapes with diurnal bloom habit that open in the midseason-to-late period. A 1958 Fairmount Garden Club note described it as 'a very light cream with wide petaled recurving blooms.' It carries no AHS awards of its own, but it entered the Reckamp breeding line as a distant ancestor of the tetraploid Minted Gold. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Early Sunrise Daylily (Very Fragrant Yellow Melon Self, Parent of Summer Splendor)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this dormant daylily, registered by Rudolph in 1963 from a cross of Frances Fay and a seedling, opens very fragrant yellow melon flowers with extended bloom habit early in the season.

directions: Registered by Rudolph in 1963 from a cross of Frances Fay and an unnamed seedling, Early Sunrise is a dormant daylily bearing a very fragrant yellow melon self flower with a melon throat, about seven inches across on 36-inch scapes with extended bloom habit that open early in the season. Carried under seedling number 60-40, it carries no AHS awards of its own. Reckamp later used it as a parent of Summer Splendor and, through that line, an ancestor of Paris Gown. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: North Star Daylily (Pale Yellow Self, Ancestor of Paris Gown)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this dormant diploid, registered by D.F. Hall in 1948, opens a pale yellow self flower in midseason on tall scapes.

directions: Registered by D.F. Hall in 1948, North Star is a dormant diploid daylily bearing a pale yellow self flower, about six inches across per a 1961 Dill Garden Club note, carried on 38-inch scapes that open in midseason. It carries no AHS awards of its own, predating the modern award system's broad adoption. As one of Hall's early postwar introductions, it later entered the multi-generation ancestry behind Reckamp's Paris Gown. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Lady of Northbrook Daylily (Cream Yellow with Pink Midrib, Ancestor of Paris Gown)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this dormant diploid, registered by Fay-Hardy in 1960, opens cream yellow flowers with a pink midrib with diurnal bloom habit in midseason.

directions: Registered by Fay-Hardy in 1960, Lady of Northbrook is a dormant diploid daylily bearing cream yellow flowers marked with a pink midrib, carried on 36-inch scapes with diurnal bloom habit that open in midseason. Catalogued under seedling number 56-11, it carries no AHS awards of its own. Its Northbrook, Illinois origin places it in the same hybridizing circle that later produced Reckamp's Paris Gown, through whose multi-generation ancestry it is credited. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Vick Mulkey Daylily (Fragrant Pink Bitone, Parent of Emerald Crown)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this fragrant dormant diploid, registered by Joiner in 1970 from a cross of Vernonburg and a seedling, opens pink bitone flowers with extended bloom habit in the midseason-to-late period.

directions: Registered by Joiner in 1970 from a cross of Vernonburg and an unnamed seedling, Vick Mulkey is a fragrant dormant diploid daylily bearing a pink bitone flower, about seven inches across on 30-inch scapes with extended bloom habit that open in the midseason-to-late period. Carried under seedling number 68-V-2, it carries no AHS awards of its own. Joiner later used it as a parent of Emerald Crown, which went on to parent the Lenington All-American Award winner Orange Velvet. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Jakarta Daylily (Light Yellow Self with Green Throat, Parent of Emerald Crown)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this reblooming dormant diploid, registered by Whatley in 1969 from a cross of Solo and a seedling, opens light yellow flowers with a green throat and extended bloom habit in the early midseason.

directions: Registered by Whatley in 1969 from a cross of Solo and an unnamed seedling, Jakarta is a reblooming dormant diploid daylily bearing a light yellow self flower with a green throat, about five inches across on 30-inch scapes with extended bloom habit that open in the early midseason. Carried under seedling number 64-Y-03, it carries no AHS awards of its own. Joiner later used it alongside Vick Mulkey as a parent of Emerald Crown, an ancestor of the Lenington All-American Award winner Orange Velvet. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Tim Tanner Daylily (Fragrant Greenish Yellow Self, Parent of Colonel Simon)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this fragrant, reblooming evergreen diploid, registered by Simon in 1965 from a cross of Grand Canyon and Southern Heritage, opens greenish yellow flowers with diurnal bloom habit very early in the season.

directions: Registered by Simon in 1965 from a cross of Grand Canyon and Southern Heritage, Tim Tanner is a fragrant, reblooming evergreen diploid daylily bearing a greenish yellow self flower, about eight inches across on 36-inch scapes with diurnal bloom habit that open very early in the season. Carried under seedling number J17-1-63-1, it carries no AHS awards of its own. L. Simon later crossed it with Clarence Simon to produce Colonel Simon, a parent of Copper Lantern and, through that line, an ancestor of Orange Velvet. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained, fertile soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Both Sides Now Daylily (Pastel Peach Coral Double, Parent of Sanford Show Girl)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil; this fragrant, reblooming evergreen diploid double, registered by D. Kirchhoff in 1985, opens pastel peach coral flowers with a rose eyezone and extended bloom habit in the early midseason.

directions: Registered by D. Kirchhoff in 1985 from a complex cross of (Siloam Double Rose x Louise Mercer) and (Double Love x Nagasaki), Both Sides Now is a fragrant, reblooming evergreen diploid double daylily bearing pastel peach coral flowers with a rose eyezone, about six inches across on 28-inch scapes with extended bloom habit that open in the early midseason. It carries no AHS awards of its own. D. Kirchhoff later crossed it with Bette Davis Eyes to produce Sanford Show Girl, a parent of Arms Reaching Out and an ancestor of the Ida Munson Award winner Mayor of Cornatzer. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained, fertile soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain its double form.

common_name: Illini Show Girl Daylily (Deep Red Self with Green Throat, Parent of Ruby Sentinel)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this dormant tetraploid, registered by Varner in 1984 from a cross of Ed Murray and Jock Randall, opens a deep red flower with a very green throat with diurnal bloom habit in midseason.

directions: Registered by Varner in 1984 from a cross of Ed Murray and Jock Randall, Illini Show Girl is a dormant tetraploid daylily bearing a deep red self flower with a very green throat, about six inches across on 32-inch scapes with diurnal bloom habit that open in midseason. Carried under seedling number So-232, it carries no AHS awards of its own. Benz later crossed it with Ed Marshall to produce Ruby Sentinel, a parent of Cherry Valentine and an ancestor of the President's Cup winner Mary Alice. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Ed Marshall Daylily (Bright Red Blend with Green Throat, Parent of Ruby Sentinel)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this dormant tetraploid, registered by Harris-Benz in 1990, opens a bright red blend flower with a brilliant green throat in midseason.

directions: Registered by Harris-Benz in 1990 from a complex cross involving Lusty Lealand and tetraploid Mavis Smith, Ed Marshall is a dormant tetraploid daylily bearing a bright red blend flower with a brilliant green throat, about five and a half inches across on 32-inch scapes that open in midseason. Carried under seedling number LMS-1, it carries no AHS awards of its own. Benz later crossed it with Illini Show Girl to produce Ruby Sentinel, a parent of Cherry Valentine and an ancestor of the President's Cup winner Mary Alice. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Frances Joiner Daylily (Fragrant Rose Blend Double, Parent of Big Kiss)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil; this fragrant, reblooming dormant diploid double, registered by Joiner in 1988, opens a rose blend flower with a green-yellow throat in midseason.

directions: Registered by Joiner in 1988, Frances Joiner is a fragrant, reblooming dormant diploid double daylily bearing a rose blend flower with a green-yellow throat, about five and a half inches across on 24-inch compact scapes that open in midseason. Carried under seedling number 84-DD-JJ-4PB, it carries no AHS awards of its own. Joiner later crossed it with Dublin Elaine to produce Big Kiss, a parent of Arms Reaching Out and an ancestor of the Ida Munson Award winner Mayor of Cornatzer. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained, fertile soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain its double form.
